title: Snake
description: Classic snake — eat, grow, avoid the wall. Self-contained, no dependencies.
controls: Arrow keys or W/A/S/D to steer; Space restarts after a game over.
howto: Steer the snake towards the food to grow longer and score points.
Avoid the walls and your own tail — either ends the run.
Every piece of food increases your length, leaving less room to turn.
Press Space (or New game) to start again.
tips: Hug the edges early so the centre stays open.
Never box yourself into a tight loop around your own body.

title: Tic-Tac-Toe
description: Minimal two-player Tic-Tac-Toe built in vanilla JS.
controls: Click a cell, or Tab to it and press Enter, to place your mark.
howto: X moves first and players alternate turns.
Line up three of your marks in a row, column or diagonal to win.
If all nine cells fill with no line, the game is a draw.
Use New game to reset the board.
tips: Take the centre — it sits on the most possible winning lines.
Always block an opponent who has two in a row.

description: Merge numbered tiles to reach 2048. Keyboard-controlled, dependency-free.
controls: Arrow keys or W/A/S/D slide every tile in that direction.
howto: Slide the tiles with the arrow keys.
Two tiles with the same number merge into their sum.
A new tile appears after every successful move.
Reach 2048 to win; the run ends when no move is possible.
tips: Keep your highest tile locked in one corner.
Avoid sliding in the direction that breaks your corner stack.

title: Memory Match
description: Flip tiles and find all eight emoji pairs. Fully keyboard accessible.
controls: Click a tile, or Tab to it and press Enter, to flip it. No mouse drag needed.
howto: Flip two tiles to look for a matching pair.
Matching pairs stay face up and are removed from play.
Tiles that do not match flip back after a moment.
Clear all eight pairs in as few moves as possible.
tips: Remember positions revealed by earlier missed flips.
Clear pairs you already know first to shrink the board.

title: Breakout
description: Bounce the ball and clear every brick. Mouse or arrow keys control the paddle.
controls: Arrow keys or the mouse move the paddle; Space starts and pauses.
howto: Keep the ball from falling past your paddle.
Bounce the ball upwards to break the brick rows.
Clear every brick to win the round.
You start with three lives.
tips: Strike the ball with the paddle edges for wider angles.
Keep an escape lane above the paddle for fast returns.

title: Pong
description: Classic Pong against a simple AI. Keyboard or mouse paddle control.
controls: Arrow keys or W/S (or the mouse) move your paddle; Space starts.
howto: Move your paddle on the left to return the ball.
An AI opponent defends the right side.
Score a point when the ball passes the opponent.
First to five points wins the match.
tips: Hit with the paddle edges to add angle to your return.
Watch the vertical speed change after each hit.

title: Minesweeper
description: Reveal safe cells without hitting a mine. Keyboard and flag mode supported.
controls: Click to reveal a cell; right-click or use Flag mode to mark a mine.
howto: Reveal a cell to see how many mines touch it.
Each number counts the mines in the eight surrounding cells.
Flag the cells you are confident about.
Reveal every safe cell to win.
tips: Open in a corner for a safer first move.
Deduce from the numbers instead of guessing.

title: Slot Games
description: Seven Blender-MCP slot machines with sticky wilds, jackpot wheels, Hold & Win and cash collect. Pick a title, set your bet and lines, then SPIN.
controls: Choose a game from the dropdown, set bet and lines, then press SPIN.
howto: Select a slot title from the top dropdown (Phoenix Fortune, Deep Sea Jackpot, Dragon Cash Hold & Win, Pirate Treasure Collect, and more).
Set your bet level and number of paylines.
Press SPIN to spin the reels and watch wins, respins, jackpots and bonus rounds animate.
Open the paytable panel to read each symbol's role and the game's special mechanics.
tips: Respins and Hold & Win rounds can chain, so let the animation finish before spinning again.
Each game's RTP is reproducible from a seed, so results are fair and auditable.
